title: Sir Gawain — Alliterative Meter
subtitle: Not iambic — Old English meter revived.
objectives: Read and translate authentic Middle English texts.

sections.heading: Content
sections.body: Not iambic pentameter. Long alliterative lines as in Old English, grouped in stanzas ending with a rhymed 'bob and wheel' (short line + four-line rhymed tail). The meter of Beowulf brought forward six hundred years. Chaucer does not use this meter; the Gawain poet does.

items.prompt: What is the focus of this lesson?
Can you apply this to reading?
items.answer: Work through examples with your notes.
